assessed_not_shipped.evidence: Audited the suite (~28 candidate `assert x == CONST`). They split into (a) LOCAL test constants — PAL/PARA/MIXED/WIDTH/BASE/TIP_KEYS, all defined in the test file (a bare-name rule false-positives on every one), and (b) CUT-imported constants — C.TIP_ID/NESTED_ID, FREQ_BAND_TOP_X, _LINK_EXTERNAL/_NAMED — which are LEGITIMATE semantic-category assertions (which overlay slot / which freq band / which link color), NOT tautologies. Flagging (b) is the DSpot trap (mutation-killing != developer-valued): it penalises GOOD symbolic-constant practice. ast-grep is syntactic — it can neither distinguish good-(b) from a true change-detector nor correlate the import that would even identify (b).

grounds: The removed `mock_run.assert_not_called()` and the new `commands_run == []` fail on the exact same condition — `subprocess.run` (resync.py:91) being invoked — since `fake_run` appends every call; the swap is behaviorally identical and adds zero detection.

The only code path a passing test exercises is the cache-hit early return (resync.py:75-76 `return out`), which contains no write to `out`; the content assertion reads back the literal 'synced content' the test itself wrote in setup.

For the content assertion to catch a mutant that `commands_run == []` misses, production would have to write `out` without calling subprocess.run on the cache path — no realistic mutation of resync() does this (dropping the branch falls through to subprocess.run at line 91, caught by commands_run; returning `src` is caught by pre-existing `result == out_srt`).

subprocess.run is mocked to a no-op that never writes the file, so even a fully broken cache branch leaves out_srt == 'synced content'; the content assertion cannot fail for any mutant that keeps commands_run green.
